subject: Archaeology
title: Piltdown Man: The Greatest Fossil Hoax
description: A short lesson to help you apply Piltdown Man: The Greatest Fossil Hoax.

hook.text: For 40 years, scientists believed a skull found in England was the missing link between apes and humans. It was a fake.

buildup.text: In 1912, Charles Dawson presented a skull from Piltdown, Sussex. It had a human-sized brain and an ape-like jaw.

discovery.text: Fluorine dating in 1953 proved the jaw was a modern orangutan's, stained and filed to look old.

twist.text: No one proved who faked it. Dawson is the main suspect, but Arthur Conan Doyle — Sherlock Holmes's creator — is also accused.

climax.text: Piltdown Man delayed real human evolution research by decades.

punchline.text: A filed orangutan jaw fooled science for 40 years.

quiz.question: What damage did the Piltdown Man hoax cause?
options: It caused museums worldwide to close their anthropology departments
It delayed real human evolution research and caused scientists to ignore genuine African fossils
It led to a permanent ban on amateur fossil hunting in England

details.summary: Piltdown Man was a forged fossil presented in 1912 as a missing link between apes and humans. A human skull was combined with an orangutan jaw and filed teeth. It took forty years for scientists to expose the hoax, revealing how bias can corrupt scientific consensus.
details.whyItMatters: Piltdown Man shows how cultural expectations — British scientists wanting a British missing link — can override scientific rigor. It remains the most famous cautionary tale in archaeology about the dangers of confirmation bias.
takeaways: A forged human skull combined with an orangutan jaw
It fooled scientists for over forty years before exposure
It demonstrates the danger of confirmation bias in science

faq.question: Who was responsible for the Piltdown hoax?
faq.answer: Charles Dawson, the amateur archaeologist who presented the find, is the primary suspect. Investigators have also implicated Arthur Conan Doyle and museum staff. The definitive perpetrator remains debated, though DNA and chemical analysis points strongest at Dawson.

faq.question: How was the Piltdown hoax eventually exposed?
faq.answer: In 1953, fluorine dating showed the skull and jaw were different ages. Microscope examination revealed filed teeth and chemical staining to fake age. Modern CT scanning and DNA analysis confirmed the jaw was from an orangutan, definitively proving the fraud.
